QUESTION:
Which other drugs interact with Prednisone?

RESPONSE:
Prednisone has multiple potential drug interactions. Common interacting drugs include: 1) CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole) which may increase prednisone levels; 2) CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine) which may decrease prednisone effectiveness; 3) Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) which may increase risk of gastrointestinal ulcers and bleeding; 4) Anticoagulants such as warfarin where prednisone may alter anticoagulant effects; 5) Vaccines, especially live vaccines, where prednisone may reduce vaccine efficacy or increase risk of infection; 6) Other immunosuppressants that may increase infection risk; and 7) Hypoglycemic agents, as prednisone can raise blood glucose levels, requiring dose adjustments. It is important to monitor for these interactions and adjust therapy accordingly.
